episodes.157280: Severe thunderstorms moved across portion of Dawes and Scotts Bluff Counties in the Panhandle during the afternoon of the 21st producing hail up to golf balls.
episodes.157325: Severe storms moved through Kimball County during the evening of the 20th producing quarter size hail and wind gust up to 60 mph.
episodes.157326: A severe thunderstorm produced up to golf ball size hail across Goshen County in the evening of the 20th.
episodes.157455: A thunderstorm produced strong wind gusts over 60 mph in the Buffalo area.
episodes.157456: A thunderstorm briefly became severe and produced hail to quarter size in New Underwood.
episodes.157457: A line of severe thunderstorms developed over eastern Pennington County and tracked northeast into western and northern portions of Haakon County. The storms produced wind gusts to 70 mph.
episodes.157458: A late night thunderstorm briefly became severe over the southern Black Hills, producing a 65 mph wind gust at the Wind Cave National Park RAWS.
episodes.157580: A deep longwave trough remained anchored over the Central and Southern Rockies on May 20th, with a deep southerly fetch of low level moisture continuing to maintain an ample moisture-rich environment over the Four State Region. Diurnal heating contributed to air mass destabilization during the afternoon, with disturbances aloft contributing to scattered shower and isolated thunderstorm development across the area. Low level shear increased during the afternoon, and helped foster the development of isolated severe thunderstorms across portions of East Texas and McCurtain County Oklahoma, with trees blown down in the community of Plunketville. Locally heavy rainfall also fell from these storms for several hours, contributing to flash flooding across McCurtain County as well. These storms eventually diminished during the late evening hours.
episodes.157581: A deep longwave trough remained anchored over the Central and Southern Rockies on May 20th, with a deep southerly fetch of low level moisture continuing to maintain an ample moisture-rich environment over the Four State Region. Diurnal heating contributed to air mass destabilization during the afternoon, with disturbances aloft contributing to scattered shower and isolated thunderstorm development across the area. Given the very moist air mass already in place, in addition to nearly saturated grounds from prior heavy rainfall, high water and flooding were reported just northeast of Many in Sabine Parish from a band of showers and thunderstorms containing locally heavy rainfall which moved repeatedly over the same areas across Western Louisiana. These storms eventually diminished from south to north by late evening.
episodes.157777: A severe thunderstorm produced very large hail over northeast Weld and northwest Logan counties.  The hail ranged in size from 2.75 to 3.25 inches in diameter.
episodes.158412: A large area of high pressure dominated the eastern US with low pressure settling across the Pacific northwest. The resultant southerly flow allowed fro deep moisture transport from the Gulf into the Midwest. A subtle disturbance in the southerly flow moved into Iowa through the afternoon and evening hours with widespread shower activity. The moisture rich environment allowed for LCLs below 500 m, combined with 0-3 km CAPE near 100 J/kg and 0-1 km SRH near 200 m2/s2. Many of the showers exhibited rotation and a couple did produce low end tornadoes and wind damage. Interestingly, the deep warm clouds within this tropical air mass resulted in no lightning with any storm the entire night.
episodes.158551: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms over a several day period resulted in widespread two to four inch rainfall across much of northeastern Oklahoma, with locally up to six inches occurring. This widespread, heavy rainfall resulted in moderate flooding of the Neosho River near Commerce.
episodes.158628: A deep mid and level trough north of the area combined with a frontal boundary near the area to result in periods of enhanced shower and thunderstorm activity. During the afternoon hours of 5/21 and 5/22, severe thunderstorms developed across interior Puerto Rico, then during the predawn hours of 5/23, an area of very heavy rainfall activity affected the coastal municipalities of eastern PR.

events.narrative: High water covered several roads in and near Eagletown. Report from a Game Warden.
Trees were downed on Welcome Home Road in the community of Plunketville. A tree also fell onto a home in this same area.
Several roads were flooded in and around Hochatown State Park. Report from Park Rangers.
A public report of wind damage within the town of Winterset with sheds blown over near the county fairgrounds. A separate personal weather station in the area reported a wind gust of 73 mph.
Tornadic Debris Signature observed on KDMX WSR-88D Doppler radar but no reports of damage, hence the EF-Unknown rating.
Weak tornado occurred south of Woodward producing minor tree damage along its path.
High water was reported on Petty Road just northeast of Many.
Wind gusts were estimated at 60 mph.
Wind gusts to 70 mph caused power outages.

The Neosho River near Commerce rose above its flood stage of 15 feet at 4:15 am CDT on May 21st. The river crested at 18.31 feet at 11:15 am CDT on the 23rd, resulting in moderate flooding. Low-lying areas around Miami were flooded, including Riverview Park, and Highway 125 near the Fairgrounds was flooded. The river fell below flood stage at 7:00 am CDT on the 24th.
A severe thunderstorm moved across the municipality of Morovis, generating strong gusty winds. Several trees and electrical poles were knocked down by the winds along Roads PR-633, 155, 159, and 567.
Quarter size hail reported in Barrio Cuchillas.
